title: Injectivity of the Razborov encoding on its auxiliary output
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, let $w$ satisfy $w > 0$, let $d$ be a natural number, and let $\gamma$ be a fixed restriction on the same $n$ variables. Consider the collection of all restrictions $\rho$ that are bad for the Boolean function computed by $f$ at depth $d$ — that is, the function $x \mapsto f(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$ — and whose Razborov encoding with parameters $w,d$ has first component equal to $\gamma$; write $S$ for the set of auxiliary lists $\mathrm{aux} \in (\bbn \times \mathrm{Bool})^{*}$ arising as the second component of the Razborov encoding of such a $\rho$. Then there exists a map $g$ from auxiliary lists to functions $\mathrm{Fin}\,d \to \mathrm{Fin}\,w \times \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Bool}$ that is injective on $S$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
the width of f is at most w
d is a natural-number depth parameter
γ is a fixed restriction on n variables
domain of injectivity: aux components of the Razborov encoding over restrictions that are bad for f's Boolean function at depth d and whose encoding has first component γ
replaced:
There exists a function $g$ from aux lists into
$\mathrm{Fin}\,d \to \mathrm{Fin}\,w \times \mathrm{Bool} \times \mathrm{Bool}$
that is injective on the image of the Razborov encoder over bad $s$-restrictions
with fixed $\gamma$. This isolates the combinatorial encoding of each of the $d$
path steps as a triple $(\mathrm{position}, \mathrm{direction}, \mathrm{hasMarker})$.
